title: Balanced and Unbalanced Forces
seo_title: Year 7 Science: Balanced and Unbalanced Forces Worksheets (Australian Curriculum)
standard_text: Investigate the effects of balanced and unbalanced forces, including Earth's gravitational force, on the motion of objects (summary of the Australian Curriculum v9.0 Science content description).
meta_desc: Free Year 7 science worksheets on balanced and unbalanced forces, resultant force, force diagrams, gravity, mass and weight. 100 questions with answers.
key_sub: Balanced forces: still or steady speed. Unbalanced: speeding up, slowing down or turning.
body_html:
How to think about it

The resultant (net) force decides what happens to an object's motion.

  • Balanced forces (resultant 0 N): the object stays still or keeps moving at a steady speed in a straight line.
  • Unbalanced forces: the object speeds up, slows down or changes direction.
  • Gravity pulls masses together. Weight (N) = mass (kg) × 9.8 N/kg on Earth; mass does not change on the Moon.
Example

Forces: 30 N right, 10 N left. Resultant?

30 − 10 = 20

Answer: 20 N to the right

Example

A car at a steady 60 km/h. Forces?

no change in speed or direction

Answer: balanced

Common mistakes

  • Thinking a moving object must have an unbalanced force.
  • Thinking balanced forces mean an object must be still.
  • Mixing up mass (kg) and weight (N).

faq.a: Forces are balanced when they are equal in size and opposite in direction, so the resultant force is zero and the motion does not change.

faq.q: How do I find a resultant force?
faq.a: Add forces acting in the same direction and subtract forces acting in opposite directions. The answer has a size and a direction.

faq.q: What is the difference between mass and weight?
faq.a: Mass is the amount of matter in an object, measured in kilograms. Weight is the force of gravity on that mass, measured in newtons.

items.q: A ute pulls a trailer with 2000 N; friction and drag are 2000 N. What happens?

items.e: Balanced forces mean no change in motion.

items.q: What does Newton's first law say?

Moving objects always slow down by themselves.
For every action there is a reaction.
items.e: This is inertia.
